How to classify a clause against a rule (this is how the reviewing team reads its own playbook):
- compliant: the clause meets the preferred position, OR it meets the fallback position on its material terms. A clause at the fallback is acceptable and is not redlined; say in the rationale that it sits at the fallback.
- deviation: the clause fails the fallback on a material term, or falls into walk-away territory. Only then propose a redline.
- missing: the rule expects a clause and no usable clause exists anywhere in the document.
- Minor sub-elements short of the preferred wording (a missing reminder mechanic, a missing price-uplift cap, 'paid' versus 'paid or payable', an accepted-but-not-preferred governing law) are noted in the rationale, not flagged as deviations.

Parties: we represent The Associated Press; counterparty is Kubient Inc..

Rule:
ID: WARRANTY
Title: Performance warranty and duration
Kind: parametric
Summary: The Vendor must stand behind its work for a meaningful period with a real remedy.
Severity: medium
Category: warranty
Position — preferred:
Services performed in a professional and workmanlike manner; deliverables/software conform to documentation for 12 months (software) or 90 days (services) with repair, replace or refund; compliance with laws; no malicious code.

Position — fallback:
90 days for software, 30 days for services; same remedies.
Position — walk-away:
"AS IS" with all warranties disclaimed and no conformance warranty at all.
Detection guidance:
Find warranty and disclaimer sections; extract the warranty period and remedy; note whether the disclaimer swallows the express warranty. A missing express warranty is a deviation (insert).

Redline guidance:
Extend the period, add the remedy sentence, carve the express warranty out of the disclaimer.
Model language:
Vendor warrants that (a) the Services will be performed in a professional and workmanlike manner consistent with industry standards; and (b) for a period of ninety (90) days following delivery, each Deliverable will conform in all material respects to its documentation. Customer's remedy for breach of this warranty is, at Vendor's option, re-performance, repair or replacement, or a refund of the fees paid for the non-conforming Services or Deliverable.

Parties: we represent The Associated Press; counterparty is Kubient Inc..

Rule:
ID: T4C
Title: Termination for convenience
Kind: parametric
Summary: We can leave on notice without penalty; the Vendor cannot walk away mid-term.
Severity: high
Category: term-termination
Position — preferred:
Customer may terminate for convenience on 30 days' written notice with a pro-rata refund of prepaid fees; Vendor has no termination-for-convenience right during a committed term.

Position — fallback:
Customer termination on 60–90 days' notice; early-termination fee not exceeding 3 months' fees; Vendor may terminate for convenience only at the end of a term on 90 days' notice.

Position — walk-away:
No Customer right to terminate for convenience in a multi-year term; Vendor termination for convenience on fewer than 90 days' notice.

Detection guidance:
Find termination provisions. Determine which party may terminate without cause, the notice period, and any early-termination fee. Absence of any Customer convenience right in a term longer than 12 months is a deviation (kind: missing behaviour); a Vendor convenience right on short notice is a deviation.

Redline guidance:
Add or edit a Customer convenience right (30 days), delete/limit Vendor's convenience right, replace penalties with the fallback fee cap.

Model language:
Customer may terminate this Agreement or any Order Form for convenience, in whole or in part, upon thirty (30) days' prior written notice to Vendor, in which case Vendor shall refund any prepaid fees for the period after the effective date of termination.

**Finding: compliant** (no redline proposed).

Paragraph 4(a) meets the T4C **fallback** on every material term:

- **AP's convenience exit** — "for any reason" on 90 days' notice after the 1-year Initial Term, within the fallback's 60–90 day band and renewing annually rather than locking AP into a multi-year term.
- **No penalty** — Kubient keeps only fees *generated during* the notice period while still delivering Services, not an early-termination fee; comfortably inside the 3-months'-fees cap.
- **Kubient's exit is not walk-away** — available only after the Initial Term and only on a full 90 days' notice.
- **Mid-term bar is symmetric** and works in our favour by stopping Kubient leaving us mid-term, so it was not flagged.

Sub-elements short of the preferred position — 90-day rather than 30-day notice, Kubient's right running any time post-Initial Term rather than only at term end, and no pro-rata prepaid-fee refund — were recorded in the rationale only. The refund point is inapplicable in any event: §5 is a revenue-share where money flows *from* Kubient to AP within 7 days of receipt, so AP prepays nothing capable of refund.

input.quote: The initial term of this Agreement shall be one (1) year from the Effective Date (the "Initial Term"). This Agreement will automatically renew for additional 1-year terms unless earlier terminated pursuant to this Agreement's express provisions (together with the Initial Term, such additional periods the "Term"). Neither Party may terminate this Agreement during the Initial Term except as set forth in paragraph 4(b) or any Exhibit. Either Party may terminate this Agreement for any reason following the Initial Term upon ninety (90) days written notice to the other Party.
input.rationale: Compliant at the playbook fallback; no redline. A Customer convenience right is expressly present: "Either Party may terminate this Agreement for any reason following the Initial Term upon ninety (90) days written notice" — a termination "for any reason" is termination for convenience, so the phrasing differs from the playbook's "for convenience" wording but is substantively identical. Ninety (90) days sits at the outer edge of the fallback's 60–90 day notice window. Term structure: a one (1) year Initial Term with 1-year auto-renewals, so the detection trigger for "absence of any Customer convenience right in a term longer than 12 months" is not met and there is no multi-year lock-in — AP has a rolling 90-day exit from the end of year one onward. The mid-Initial-Term bar ("Neither Party may terminate ... during the Initial Term") is symmetric and equally restrains Kubient from walking away on AP mid-term, so it partly benefits our party and is not flagged. No early-termination fee or penalty falls on AP: Kubient is entitled only to fees "generated during the termination period," i.e. revenue actually earned across the 90-day notice period while it continues performing, which is within the fallback's 3-months'-fees cap rather than a penalty. Vendor convenience right is available only following the Initial Term and on exactly ninety (90) days' notice — not "fewer than 90 days" — so it stays out of walk-away territory. Sub-elements short of the preferred position, noted rather than escalated per the playbook's classification semantics: 90-day rather than 30-day notice; Kubient's right running any time after the Initial Term rather than only at the end of a renewal term; and no pro-rata refund of prepaid fees, which is inapplicable because §5 (p0023) is a revenue-share under which payments flow from Kubient to AP within 7 days of receipt, so AP prepays nothing capable of refund.

input.quote: Kubient hereby grants to Customer a limited, royalty-free, non-exclusive, non-transferable, non-assignable, without right of sublicense, revocable license to access, participate in and use to the full extent the Auction Platform as hosted by Kubient,
input.rationale: The grant in paragraph 2 is expressly "revocable" with no qualification, so on its face Kubient may revoke at its discretion (paragraph 4(c)(ii) only confirms revocation on termination; it does not limit revocation to that event). The grant names only Customer — no AP affiliates or contractors — and paragraph 8(a) affirmatively bars third-party access to the Service absent Kubient's prior written approval, leaving no path to add them. That combination (revocable at Vendor's discretion plus affiliates/contractors excluded with no path to add) is the rule's walk-away case and fails the fallback, which requires at minimum affiliate coverage on notice. The transfer prong is largely satisfied outside the grant: paragraph 14(h) permits assignment of the Agreement to an affiliate or M&A successor, though the grant itself remains "non-transferable, non-assignable". Redline extends the licence to affiliates and contractors acting on our behalf (with AP remaining responsible for their compliance), limits revocation to expiration or termination under paragraph 4, and conforms transferability to paragraph 14(h).

proposal.summary: Extend the Auction Platform licence to AP affiliates and contractors, remove at-will revocability, and permit transfer to a successor.
proposal.comment: [Playbook] We extended the licence to our affiliates and to contractors acting on our behalf, tied revocation to expiration or termination under paragraph 4 rather than Kubient's discretion, and aligned transferability with the assignment right in paragraph 14(h). A licence that is revocable at will and excludes affiliates and contractors is not workable for us operationally.

input.quote: Kubient hereby grants to Customer a limited, royalty-free, non-exclusive, non-transferable, non-assignable, without right of sublicense, revocable license to access, participate in and use to the full extent the Auction Platform as hosted by Kubient,
input.rationale: The grant in paragraph 2 is expressly "revocable" with no qualification, so on its face Kubient may revoke at its discretion (paragraph 4(c)(ii) only confirms revocation on termination; it does not limit revocation to that event). The grant names only Customer — no AP affiliates or contractors — and paragraph 8(a) affirmatively bars third-party access to the Service absent Kubient's prior written approval, leaving no path to add them. That combination (revocable at Vendor's discretion plus affiliates/contractors excluded with no path to add) is the rule's walk-away case and fails the fallback, which requires at minimum affiliate coverage on notice. The transfer prong is largely satisfied outside the grant: paragraph 14(h) permits assignment of the Agreement to an affiliate or M&A successor, though the grant itself remains "non-transferable, non-assignable". Redline extends the licence to affiliates and contractors acting on our behalf (with AP remaining responsible for their compliance), limits revocation to expiration or termination under paragraph 4, and conforms transferability to paragraph 14(h).

Rule:
ID: AUDIT
Title: Audit rights against Customer
Kind: parametric
Summary: Audits of our usage must be rare, notified, off-site where possible and at the Vendor's cost.
Severity: medium
Category: audit
Position — preferred:
No more than once per 12 months, on 30 days' written notice, during business hours, by an independent auditor bound by confidentiality, at Vendor's cost unless underpayment exceeds 5 %; no direct access to Customer systems.

Position — fallback:
Once per year on 15 days' notice; Vendor bears cost unless underpayment exceeds 10 %.
Position — walk-away:
Unlimited or unannounced audits, or remote access to Customer systems.
Detection guidance:
Find audit/inspection/verification rights binding Customer; extract frequency, notice, cost allocation, system access.
Redline guidance:
Insert the frequency/notice/cost limits with minimal edits; delete system-access language.

Claimed finding status: compliant

Finding rationale:
Compliant. The Agreement grants Kubient no audit, inspection, verification or records-examination right over AP. Full-text searches for "audit", "inspect", "records" and "verif" return no hits, and a read of the entire Master Services Agreement (single section, p0000-p0074) confirms no such right exists. The only access-flavoured obligation is Section 1 (p0001), where AP agrees to provide "reasonable and necessary access, support and cooperation for Kubient to provide the Services" — a service-enablement cooperation covenant, not a right to examine AP's books, usage or systems. Direction check: this rule exists to cap a Vendor right that is adverse to us; its complete absence is more favourable to AP than the preferred position (once per 12 months, 30 days' written notice, independent auditor under confidentiality, Vendor cost unless underpayment exceeds 5%, no system access), so there is nothing to limit and no redline is warranted. The deterministic "audit frequency limited" check fails only because there is no audit clause to carry a frequency cap — not because audits are unlimited or unannounced, so this is not walk-away territory. A "missing" finding would also be wrong: the rule is a constraint on a Vendor right, not an entitlement we need to procure. Commercially this fits the bargain, since fees flow from Kubient to AP under a revenue share with sequential liability (Section 5, p0023), leaving no AP usage or underpayment for Kubient to audit. Residual internal note: Exhibits are incorporated into the Agreement under Section 1, so if any Exhibit or amendment later introduces audit or system-access language we should require the preferred parameters at that point.

Original paragraphs:
p0001: 1. Kubient Services. The services provided by Kubient pursuant to each specific engagement by Customer (the "Service" or "Services") shall be set forth and detailed in individual exhibits attached hereto (each an "Exhibit"), which shall be subject to the terms and conditions hereof and be incorporated as part of this Agreement. Kubient shall use reasonable efforts to provide to Customer the Services. Customer agrees to provide all reasonable and necessary access, support and cooperation for Kubient to provide the Services in a timely and effective manner. Nothing herein is intended nor shall be construed as creating an exclusive arrangement between Customer and Kubient. This Agreement will not restrict Customer offering Inventory via other agents or otherwise selling Inventory to any third parties.

Resolved definitions:
Agreement: Exhibit 10.14 MASTER SERVICES AGREEMENT This Master Services Agreement (the "Agreement"), dated as of the 5th day of February, 2020 (the "Effective Date"), is by and between Kubient Inc., with offices located at 330 7th Avenue, 10th Floor, New York, NY 10001 ("Kubient") and The Associated Press, a New York not-for-profit corporation with principal place of business located at 200 Liberty Street, New York, NY 10281 (the "Customer"). Parties: we represent The Associated Press; counterparty is Kubient Inc..

Rule:
ID: WARRANTY
Title: Performance warranty and duration
Kind: parametric
Summary: The Vendor must stand behind its work for a meaningful period with a real remedy.
Severity: medium
Category: warranty
Position — preferred:
Services performed in a professional and workmanlike manner; deliverables/software conform to documentation for 12 months (software) or 90 days (services) with repair, replace or refund; compliance with laws; no malicious code.

Position — fallback:
90 days for software, 30 days for services; same remedies.
Position — walk-away:
"AS IS" with all warranties disclaimed and no conformance warranty at all.
Detection guidance:
Find warranty and disclaimer sections; extract the warranty period and remedy; note whether the disclaimer swallows the express warranty. A missing express warranty is a deviation (insert).

Redline guidance:
Extend the period, add the remedy sentence, carve the express warranty out of the disclaimer.
Model language:
Vendor warrants that (a) the Services will be performed in a professional and workmanlike manner consistent with industry standards; and (b) for a period of ninety (90) days following delivery, each Deliverable will conform in all material respects to its documentation. Customer's remedy for breach of this warranty is, at Vendor's option, re-performance, repair or replacement, or a refund of the fees paid for the non-conforming Services or Deliverable.

input.rationale: Section 9(b) contains a genuine express performance warranty from Kubient that meets and exceeds our preferred position on the material terms: the Service will perform in all material respects to industry standards (p0034), services will comply with the Agreement and be "free from errors that materially affect their utility" (p0038), the product and service will be free of viruses, Trojan Horses, worms, back doors and similar malicious routines (p0036), and Kubient will comply with all applicable Laws throughout the Term (p0041). Duration is better than preferred: these are continuing warranties/covenants running for the whole Term rather than a 12-month or 90-day window. The Section 13 disclaimer does not swallow the express warranty — it is twice qualified ("Except as expressly set forth herein" and "except for the representations and warranties set forth in this Agreement"), so it disclaims only implied warranties and the revenue/profit guarantee, and does not reach walk-away "AS IS" territory. Noted but not flagged: there is no express repair/re-perform/refund remedy sentence. That is a sub-element short of the preferred wording only, and its absence works in our favour — we keep our full contractual remedies (direct damages, plus termination on 30 days' uncured material breach under 4(b)) rather than being confined to a capped exclusive remedy. No redline warranted.

(h) "Target Demand" means the Registered Bidder that has placed a Bid for Impressions to be delivered in Inventory.
(i) "Inventory" means advertising space on, within or associated with premium content on web site(s) or app(s) offered through the Auction Platform by Customer.

Use the document tools to inspect only the clauses needed, including definitions and cross-references.
Reason about direction: identify who is bound and do not flag obligations that benefit our party.
Every quote and replace.oldText must be a verbatim substring from a tool response. Quotes must be 600 characters or fewer.
Apply the playbook's classification semantics: a clause that meets the preferred or the fallback position on its material terms is compliant — do not redline it. When a clause genuinely fails the fallback, make the smallest edit that reaches the preferred position; use fallback language only when the rule guidance or the existing bargain makes preferred disproportionate.
Comments must begin with the supplied playbook prefix, use concise first-person-plural language, and explain the change and reason.
For deviation or missing findings, call propose_redline and obtain ok:true before submit_finding.
For compliant findings, do not propose a redline. Call submit_finding exactly once, then stop calling tools.

We represent the customer.
Our party aliases: Customer, Client, Licensee, Company, Buyer, Purchaser, Subscriber, User.
Counterparty aliases: Vendor, Supplier, Provider, Service Provider, Licensor, Contractor, Consultant, Seller, Host.
Comment prefix: [Playbook].
Tone: Concise, professional, first person plural ("we"). Explain what changed and why in one or two sentences, cite the playbook position, offer the fallback where sensible, never lecture.


How to classify a clause against a rule (this is how the reviewing team reads its own playbook):
- compliant: the clause meets the preferred position, OR it meets the fallback position on its material terms. A clause at the fallback is acceptable and is not redlined; say in the rationale that it sits at the fallback.
- deviation: the clause fails the fallback on a material term, or falls into walk-away territory. Only then propose a redline.
- missing: the rule expects a clause and no usable clause exists anywhere in the document.
- Minor sub-elements short of the preferred wording (a missing reminder mechanic, a missing price-uplift cap, 'paid' versus 'paid or payable', an accepted-but-not-preferred governing law) are noted in the rationale, not flagged as deviations.
- Do not flag a clause that benefits our party. Do not flag the same commercial term twice under two rules unless both rules are independently breached.

Rule:
ID: INSURANCE
Title: Vendor insurance
Kind: missing
Summary: Vendors that touch our data or premises carry standard insurance.
Severity: low
Category: insurance
Position — preferred:
Commercial general liability USD 1M per occurrence / 2M aggregate; professional (E&O) USD 2M; cyber/privacy USD 5M for vendors processing Customer Data; workers' compensation as required by law; certificates on request.

Position — fallback:
E&O USD 1M and cyber USD 2M.
Position — walk-away:
No insurance for a vendor that processes personal data or works on our premises.
Detection guidance:
Look for an insurance clause; if absent for a services/hosting vendor, deviation (insert).
Redline guidance:
Insert a short insurance paragraph in the general/miscellaneous section.
Model language:
Vendor shall maintain, at its own expense, throughout the term and for one (1) year thereafter: commercial general liability insurance of not less than USD 1,000,000 per occurrence and USD 2,000,000 in the aggregate; professional liability (errors and omissions) insurance of not less than USD 2,000,000; and, where Vendor processes Customer Data, cyber liability insurance of not less than USD 5,000,000. Vendor shall provide certificates of insurance on request.

Title: Minimum purchase commitments and volume restrictions on Customer

Parties: we represent The Associated Press; counterparty is Kubient Inc..

Rule:
ID: INSURANCE
Title: Vendor insurance
Kind: missing
Summary: Vendors that touch our data or premises carry standard insurance.
Severity: low
Category: insurance
Position — preferred:
Commercial general liability USD 1M per occurrence / 2M aggregate; professional (E&O) USD 2M; cyber/privacy USD 5M for vendors processing Customer Data; workers' compensation as required by law; certificates on request.

Position — fallback:
E&O USD 1M and cyber USD 2M.
Position — walk-away:
No insurance for a vendor that processes personal data or works on our premises.
Detection guidance:
Look for an insurance clause; if absent for a services/hosting vendor, deviation (insert).
Redline guidance:
Insert a short insurance paragraph in the general/miscellaneous section.
Model language:
Vendor shall maintain, at its own expense, throughout the term and for one (1) year thereafter: commercial general liability insurance of not less than USD 1,000,000 per occurrence and USD 2,000,000 in the aggregate; professional liability (errors and omissions) insurance of not less than USD 2,000,000; and, where Vendor processes Customer Data, cyber liability insurance of not less than USD 5,000,000. Vendor shall provide certificates of insurance on request.

**Finding: Compliant** — no redline proposed.

The warranty package in Section 9(b) meets and in places exceeds our preferred position:

- **Performance warranty present**: Service will "perform in all material respects to industry standards" (p0034) and services will be "free from errors that materially affect their utility" (p0038) — the functional equivalent of professional/workmanlike plus conformance.
- **Duration better than preferred**: these are continuing warranties/covenants for the entire Term, not a 12-month or 90-day window.
- **Compliance with laws** (p0041) and **no malicious code** (p0036) are both expressly covered.
- **Disclaimer does not swallow the warranty**: Section 13 is double-qualified ("Except as expressly set forth herein" / "except for the representations and warranties set forth in this Agreement"), so it reaches only implied warranties and the revenue/profit guarantee — nowhere near walk-away "AS IS".

Noted in the rationale but deliberately not flagged: there is no express repair/re-perform/refund remedy sentence. That is a sub-element short of the preferred wording, and its absence favours us — we retain full direct-damages recovery and the 30-day cure/termination right under 4(b) instead of being confined to an exclusive, capped remedy. Inserting the model remedy language would risk narrowing our position, so I left it alone.

system.text:
You are an independent verifier of one proposed contract finding.
Judge the proposal against the supplied playbook rule, original paragraphs, resolved definitions, deterministic checks, rendered redline, and comment.
Do not rely on hidden drafter reasoning. Fail invalid, directionally wrong, or rule-incomplete edits.
Deterministic checks are heuristics (regular expressions and a changed-character ratio), not verdicts: a failed regex may simply be a phrasing variant, and a high changed-character ratio is acceptable when the rule genuinely requires rewriting the clause (for example replacing a governing-law sentence or deleting a take-or-pay obligation). Weigh them as evidence and decide on substance: does the redline reach the playbook position with the smallest edit that does so, and is the comment accurate?
The claimed status matters: for a compliant finding, no redline or counterparty comment is expected, and you should pass when the cited text supports compliance. Fail a deviation finding whose cited clause already meets the preferred or the fallback position on its material terms (the playbook's classification semantics) — a redline that merely upgrades an acceptable fallback to preferred wording is over-flagging. Compliant findings are retained as internal evaluation evidence, not raised as negotiation issues. For deviation or missing findings, require an actionable valid proposal.
Return a concise verdict with actionable reasons.

We represent the customer.
Our party aliases: Customer, Client, Licensee, Company, Buyer, Purchaser, Subscriber, User.
Counterparty aliases: Vendor, Supplier, Provider, Service Provider, Licensor, Contractor, Consultant, Seller, Host.
Comment prefix: [Playbook].
Tone: Concise, professional, first person plural ("we"). Explain what changed and why in one or two sentences, cite the playbook position, offer the fallback where sensible, never lecture.


How to classify a clause against a rule (this is how the reviewing team reads its own playbook):
- compliant: the clause meets the preferred position, OR it meets the fallback position on its material terms. A clause at the fallback is acceptable and is not redlined; say in the rationale that it sits at the fallback.
- deviation: the clause fails the fallback on a material term, or falls into walk-away territory. Only then propose a redline.
- missing: the rule expects a clause and no usable clause exists anywhere in the document.
- Minor sub-elements short of the preferred wording (a missing reminder mechanic, a missing price-uplift cap, 'paid' versus 'paid or payable', an accepted-but-not-preferred governing law) are noted in the rationale, not flagged as deviations.
- Do not flag a clause that benefits our party. Do not flag the same commercial term twice under two rules unless both rules are independently breached.

Rule:
ID: WARRANTY
Title: Performance warranty and duration
Kind: parametric
Summary: The Vendor must stand behind its work for a meaningful period with a real remedy.
Severity: medium
Category: warranty
Position — preferred:
Services performed in a professional and workmanlike manner; deliverables/software conform to documentation for 12 months (software) or 90 days (services) with repair, replace or refund; compliance with laws; no malicious code.

Position — fallback:
90 days for software, 30 days for services; same remedies.
Position — walk-away:
"AS IS" with all warranties disclaimed and no conformance warranty at all.
Detection guidance:
Find warranty and disclaimer sections; extract the warranty period and remedy; note whether the disclaimer swallows the express warranty. A missing express warranty is a deviation (insert).

Redline guidance:
Extend the period, add the remedy sentence, carve the express warranty out of the disclaimer.
Model language:
Vendor warrants that (a) the Services will be performed in a professional and workmanlike manner consistent with industry standards; and (b) for a period of ninety (90) days following delivery, each Deliverable will conform in all material respects to its documentation. Customer's remedy for breach of this warranty is, at Vendor's option, re-performance, repair or replacement, or a refund of the fees paid for the non-conforming Services or Deliverable.


Claimed finding status: compliant

Finding rationale:
Section 9(b) contains a genuine express performance warranty from Kubient that meets and exceeds our preferred position on the material terms: the Service will perform in all material respects to industry standards (p0034), services will comply with the Agreement and be "free from errors that materially affect their utility" (p0038), the product and service will be free of viruses, Trojan Horses, worms, back doors and similar malicious routines (p0036), and Kubient will comply with all applicable Laws throughout the Term (p0041). Duration is better than preferred: these are continuing warranties/covenants running for the whole Term rather than a 12-month or 90-day window. The Section 13 disclaimer does not swallow the express warranty — it is twice qualified ("Except as expressly set forth herein" and "except for the representations and warranties set forth in this Agreement"), so it disclaims only implied warranties and the revenue/profit guarantee, and does not reach walk-away "AS IS" territory. Noted but not flagged: there is no express repair/re-perform/refund remedy sentence. That is a sub-element short of the preferred wording only, and its absence works in our favour — we keep our full contractual remedies (direct damages, plus termination on 30 days' uncured material breach under 4(b)) rather than being confined to a capped exclusive remedy. No redline warranted.

You are a precise customer-side contract drafter handling one playbook rule.
Use the document tools to inspect only the clauses needed, including definitions and cross-references.
Reason about direction: identify who is bound and do not flag obligations that benefit our party.
Every quote and replace.oldText must be a verbatim substring from a tool response. Quotes must be 600 characters or fewer.
Apply the playbook's classification semantics: a clause that meets the preferred or the fallback position on its material terms is compliant — do not redline it. When a clause genuinely fails the fallback, make the smallest edit that reaches the preferred position; use fallback language only when the rule guidance or the existing bargain makes preferred disproportionate.
Comments must begin with the supplied playbook prefix, use concise first-person-plural language, and explain the change and reason.
For deviation or missing findings, call propose_redline and obtain ok:true before submit_finding.
For compliant findings, do not propose a redline. Call submit_finding exactly once, then stop calling tools.

We represent the customer.
Our party aliases: Customer, Client, Licensee, Company, Buyer, Purchaser, Subscriber, User.
Counterparty aliases: Vendor, Supplier, Provider, Service Provider, Licensor, Contractor, Consultant, Seller, Host.
Comment prefix: [Playbook].
Tone: Concise, professional, first person plural ("we"). Explain what changed and why in one or two sentences, cite the playbook position, offer the fallback where sensible, never lecture.


How to classify a clause against a rule (this is how the reviewing team reads its own playbook):
- compliant: the clause meets the preferred position, OR it meets the fallback position on its material terms. A clause at the fallback is acceptable and is not redlined; say in the rationale that it sits at the fallback.
- deviation: the clause fails the fallback on a material term, or falls into walk-away territory. Only then propose a redline.
- missing: the rule expects a clause and no usable clause exists anywhere in the document.
- Minor sub-elements short of the preferred wording (a missing reminder mechanic, a missing price-uplift cap, 'paid' versus 'paid or payable', an accepted-but-not-preferred governing law) are noted in the rationale, not flagged as deviations.
- Do not flag a clause that benefits our party. Do not flag the same commercial term twice under two rules unless both rules are independently breached.

Parties: we represent The Associated Press; counterparty is Kubient Inc..

Rule:
ID: AUDIT
Title: Audit rights against Customer
Kind: parametric
Summary: Audits of our usage must be rare, notified, off-site where possible and at the Vendor's cost.
Severity: medium
Category: audit
Position — preferred:
No more than once per 12 months, on 30 days' written notice, during business hours, by an independent auditor bound by confidentiality, at Vendor's cost unless underpayment exceeds 5 %; no direct access to Customer systems.

Position — fallback:
Once per year on 15 days' notice; Vendor bears cost unless underpayment exceeds 10 %.
Position — walk-away:
Unlimited or unannounced audits, or remote access to Customer systems.
Detection guidance:
Find audit/inspection/verification rights binding Customer; extract frequency, notice, cost allocation, system access.
Redline guidance:
Insert the frequency/notice/cost limits with minimal edits; delete system-access language.

input.rationale: The Agreement grants Kubient no audit, inspection, verification or records-examination right over the Customer (AP). 4. Term and Termination.

(a) The initial term of this Agreement shall be one (1) year from the Effective Date (the "Initial Term"). This Agreement will automatically renew for additional 1-year terms unless earlier terminated pursuant to this Agreement's express provisions (together with the Initial Term, such additional periods the "Term"). Neither Party may terminate this Agreement during the Initial Term except as set forth in paragraph 4(b) or any Exhibit. Either Party may terminate this Agreement for any reason following the Initial Term upon ninety (90) days written notice to the other Party. Except for termination for material breach as detailed in paragraph 4(b), Kubient shall be entitled to all fees generated during the termination period regardless of which Party terminates the Agreement, (b) Either Party may terminate this Agreement if the other Party commits a material breach of the Agreement and upon thirty (30) days written notice to the other Party, such other Party hasn't cured the breach within such thirty (30) days. Either Party may terminate the Agreement immediately if the other party (i) becomes insolvent or makes a general assignment for the benefit of creditors;

5. Fees and Payment. The Parties agree to share any revenue generated as a result of this Agreement, or Customer's use of the Services or the Auction Platform, as set forth and detailed in each applicable Exhibit. Unless specified otherwise in an Exhibit, Kubient shall be responsible for contracting with all advertisers, agencies, media buyers, and/or sponsors (collectively "Advertisers") on Customer's behalf, including Advertisers with whom Customer has existing relationships. Pursuant to the doctrine of sequential liability, payment from Kubient to Customer shall be made within seven (7) days from Kubient's receipt of payment, regardless of when Customer submits an invoice. Customer acknowledges and agrees that Kubient shall proceed with recovery of the amounts due on a best effort basis but will not initiate any legal action against a delinquent party without the express written consent and support of Customer. Except of taxes associated with Kubient's income, Customer shall be responsible for paying all applicable sales, use or other taxes, duties, or tariffs applicable to its use of the Services.
6. Use of Service.

(a) Customer will comply with all international, federal, state and local laws, rules, and regulations of any governmental or regulating authority ("Law") that are applicable to its business and use of the Service. Customer agrees that it will not transfer or (unless expressly and specifically approved by Kubient in advance and in writing) allow third-party access to the Service. Customer shall be responsible and solely liable for all the Content (including without limitation all intellectual property rights therein) and the Properties.

(a) EXCEPT WITH RESPECT TO THE PARTIES' LIABILITY FOR INDEMNIFICATION, OR LIABILITY FOR BREACH OF CONFIDENTIALITY, NEITHER PARTY SHALL BE LIABLE FOR ANY CONSEQUENTIAL, INCIDENTAL, INDIRECT, PUNITIVE, SPECIAL OR OTHER SIMILAR DAMAGES, WHETHER OR NOT CAUSED BY THE OTHER PARTY'S EMPLOYEES OR REPRESENTATIVES„ WHETHER UNDER TORT (INCLUDING NEGLIGENCE), CONTRACT OR OTHER THEORIES OF RECOVERY, EVEN IF THE OTHER PARTY WAS OR SHOULD HAVE BEEN AWARE OR WAS ADVISED OF THE POSSIBILITY OF SUCH DAMAGES.

Each Party agrees and does waive trial by jury in any action, proceeding or counterclaim brought against the other Party for any matter whatsoever arising out of or in any way connected with this Agreement. No action, suit or proceeding shall be brought against a Party more than one year after the date of termination this Agreement. Any controversy or claim arising out of or relating to this Agreement, or the breach thereof, shall be settled by arbitration administered by the American Arbitration Association under its Commercial Arbitration Rules, and judgment on the award rendered by the arbitrator(s) may be entered in any court having jurisdiction thereof

content.text:
**Finding submitted: deviation (high severity) — LICENSE / Licence grant scope**

**What the document says.** Paragraph 2 grants AP "a limited, royalty-free, non-exclusive, non-transferable, non-assignable, without right of sublicense, **revocable** license" to the Auction Platform, in AP's name only.

**Why it fails the fallback.**
1. **Revocability** — "revocable" is unqualified, so Kubient can revoke at will. Paragraph 4(c)(ii) says the licence "shall be revoked" on termination, but that confirms one revocation trigger rather than limiting revocation to it.
2. **Affiliates/contractors excluded with no path to add** — the grant runs to "Customer" alone, and paragraph 8(a) separately bars AP from allowing "third-party access to the Service" without Kubient's prior written approval. Together these are the rule's walk-away scenario.
3. **Transfer** — largely covered elsewhere: paragraph 14(h) allows either party to assign to an affiliate or M&A successor without consent. Noted, not separately flagged, though the grant clause itself still reads "non-transferable, non-assignable."

**Redline (validated ok:true).** Two conforming edits:
- Paragraph 2: grant runs to "Customer, its affiliates and its contractors acting on its behalf"; "non-transferable, non-assignable" and bare "revocable" replaced with "transferable to a successor in accordance with paragraph 14(h) and revocable only upon expiration or termination of this Agreement in accordance with paragraph 4."
- Paragraph 8(a): carve-out so the third-party access ban does not swallow the new affiliate/contractor scope, with AP remaining responsible for their compliance — this concession keeps the edit acceptable to Kubient.

The paragraph 8(a) edit is worth a word of explanation, since a strictly minimal redline would touch only the grant. Amending paragraph 2 alone would leave the affiliate and contractor extension self-defeating, because paragraph 8(a) independently prohibits the very access the new grant language permits. The two edits are one substantive change.

One item for your confirmation: I read paragraph 4(c)(ii)'s reference to "the license granted under section 3" as a mis-citation, since the licence is granted in section 2 and section 3 contains only definitions. My redline cross-references paragraph 4 for revocation and paragraph 14(h) for transfer, so it does not depend on that reference being corrected — but you may want to fix the numbering in the same turn.

system.text:
You are an independent verifier of one proposed contract finding.
Judge the proposal against the supplied playbook rule, original paragraphs, resolved definitions, deterministic checks, rendered redline, and comment.
Do not rely on hidden drafter reasoning. Fail invalid, directionally wrong, or rule-incomplete edits.
Deterministic checks are heuristics (regular expressions and a changed-character ratio), not verdicts: a failed regex may simply be a phrasing variant, and a high changed-character ratio is acceptable when the rule genuinely requires rewriting the clause (for example replacing a governing-law sentence or deleting a take-or-pay obligation). Weigh them as evidence and decide on substance: does the redline reach the playbook position with the smallest edit that does so, and is the comment accurate?
The claimed status matters: for a compliant finding, no redline or counterparty comment is expected, and you should pass when the cited text supports compliance. Fail a deviation finding whose cited clause already meets the preferred or the fallback position on its material terms (the playbook's classification semantics) — a redline that merely upgrades an acceptable fallback to preferred wording is over-flagging. Compliant findings are retained as internal evaluation evidence, not raised as negotiation issues. For deviation or missing findings, require an actionable valid proposal.
Return a concise verdict with actionable reasons.

Our party aliases: Customer, Client, Licensee, Company, Buyer, Purchaser, Subscriber, User.
Counterparty aliases: Vendor, Supplier, Provider, Service Provider, Licensor, Contractor, Consultant, Seller, Host.
Comment prefix: [Playbook].
Tone: Concise, professional, first person plural ("we"). Explain what changed and why in one or two sentences, cite the playbook position, offer the fallback where sensible, never lecture.


How to classify a clause against a rule (this is how the reviewing team reads its own playbook):
- compliant: the clause meets the preferred position, OR it meets the fallback position on its material terms. A clause at the fallback is acceptable and is not redlined; say in the rationale that it sits at the fallback.
- deviation: the clause fails the fallback on a material term, or falls into walk-away territory. Only then propose a redline.
- missing: the rule expects a clause and no usable clause exists anywhere in the document.
- Minor sub-elements short of the preferred wording (a missing reminder mechanic, a missing price-uplift cap, 'paid' versus 'paid or payable', an accepted-but-not-preferred governing law) are noted in the rationale, not flagged as deviations.
- Do not flag a clause that benefits our party. Do not flag the same commercial term twice under two rules unless both rules are independently breached.

messages.content:
Rule:
ID: LICENSE
Title: Licence grant scope
Kind: parametric
Summary: The licence must cover our affiliates and contractors and must not be revocable at will.
Severity: high
Category: licence
Position — preferred:
Licence extends to Customer's affiliates and to contractors acting on Customer's behalf; paid-up licences are perpetual and irrevocable; subscription licences terminable only for uncured material breach; transferable to successors.

Position — fallback:
Affiliates covered on written notice; transferable to a successor in an M&A transaction.
Position — walk-away:
Licence revocable at Vendor's discretion; affiliates and contractors excluded with no path to add them.
Detection guidance:
Find the grant clause: "non-exclusive, non-transferable", "revocable", "solely for Customer's internal use", whether affiliates/contractors are named, term of the licence.

Redline guidance:
Insert "and its Affiliates and contractors acting on its behalf", delete "revocable", add successor transfer.

Claimed finding status: deviation

Finding rationale:
The grant in paragraph 2 is expressly "revocable" with no qualification, so on its face Kubient may revoke at its discretion (paragraph 4(c)(ii) only confirms revocation on termination; it does not limit revocation to that event). The grant names only Customer — no AP affiliates or contractors — and paragraph 8(a) affirmatively bars third-party access to the Service absent Kubient's prior written approval, leaving no path to add them. That combination (revocable at Vendor's discretion plus affiliates/contractors excluded with no path to add) is the rule's walk-away case and fails the fallback, which requires at minimum affiliate coverage on notice. The transfer prong is largely satisfied outside the grant: paragraph 14(h) permits assignment of the Agreement to an affiliate or M&A successor, though the grant itself remains "non-transferable, non-assignable". Redline extends the licence to affiliates and contractors acting on our behalf (with AP remaining responsible for their compliance), limits revocation to expiration or termination under paragraph 4, and conforms transferability to paragraph 14(h).

Original paragraphs:
p0002: 2. Kubient License. In the event Customer shall utilize Kubient's ad serving technology as part of the Services, Kubient hereby grants to Customer a limited, royalty-free, non-exclusive, non-transferable, non-assignable, without right of sublicense, revocable license to access, participate in and use to the full extent the Auction Platform as hosted by Kubient, for the purpose of serving Inventory at Target Demand (" "). The Auction Platform will place Creative from the Target Demand with the Winning Bid Price on Google Ad Manager for such Creative to be placed on Customer's websites.
p0025: (a) Customer will comply with all international, federal, state and local laws, rules, and regulations of any governmental or regulating authority ("Law") that are applicable to its business and use of the Service. Customer agrees that it will not transfer or (unless expressly and specifically approved by Kubient in advance and in writing) allow third-party access to the Service. Customer will not modify, translate, alter, tamper with, repair, or otherwise create derivative works of any software included in any Service; reverse engineer, disassemble, or decompile any software or Service or apply any other process or procedure to derive source code of any software included in any Service; or resell, transfer, assign, or use as a service bureau any Service. Customer will ensure that its stories, articles, polls, videos, pictures, photographs, images, broadcasts, and any other type of content (collectively the "Content"), and each of its websites, devices, applications, podcasts, ads, emails, databases or any other types of mediums for which the Service is engaged (collectively the "Properties") contains or is linked to a privacy policy in accordance with applicable Law. Customer shall be responsible and solely liable for all the Content (including without limitation all intellectual property rights therein) and the Properties.

Resolved definitions:
Customer: Exhibit 10.14 MASTER SERVICES AGREEMENT This Master Services Agreement (the "Agreement"), dated as of the 5th day of February, 2020 (the "Effective Date"), is by and between Kubient Inc., with offices located at 330 7th Avenue, 10th Floor, New York, NY 10001 ("Kubient") and The Associated Press, a New York not-for-profit corporation with principal place of business located at 200 Liberty Street, New York, NY 10281 (the "Customer"). Each of Customer and Kubient may be referred to herein individually as a "Party" and collectively as the "Parties". WHEREAS, Customer wishes to increase the revenue derived from its traffic, content, websites, applications, podcasts, audience and database, and would like to retain Kubient to support and assist in that process as described herein; For good and valuable consideration, the receipt of which is acknowledged by each Party, the Parties agree as follows:

Rendered redline:
p0002: 2. Kubient License. In the event Customer shall utilize Kubient's ad serving technology as part of the Services, Kubient hereby grants to Customer, its affiliates and its contractors acting on its behalf a limited, royalty-free, non-exclusive license, without right of sublicense, transferable to a successor in accordance with paragraph 14(h) and revocable only upon expiration or termination of this Agreement in accordance with paragraph 4, to access, participate in and use to the full extent the Auction Platform as hosted by Kubient, for the purpose of serving Inventory at Target Demand (" "). The Auction Platform will place Creative from the Target Demand with the Winning Bid Price on Google Ad Manager for such Creative to be placed on Customer's websites.
p0025: (a) Customer will comply with all international, federal, state and local laws, rules, and regulations of any governmental or regulating authority ("Law") that are applicable to its business and use of the Service. Customer agrees that it will not transfer or (unless expressly and specifically approved by Kubient in advance and in writing) allow third-party access to the Service, other than access by Customer's affiliates and contractors acting on Customer's behalf as permitted under paragraph 2, for whose compliance with this Agreement Customer shall remain responsible. Customer will not modify, translate, alter, tamper with, repair, or otherwise create derivative works of any software included in any Service; reverse engineer, disassemble, or decompile any software or Service or apply any other process or procedure to derive source code of any software included in any Service; or resell, transfer, assign, or use as a service bureau any Service. Customer will ensure that its stories, articles, polls, videos, pictures, photographs, images, broadcasts, and any other type of content (collectively the "Content"), and each of its websites, devices, applications, podcasts, ads, emails, databases or any other types of mediums for which the Service is engaged (collectively the "Properties") contains or is linked to a privacy policy in accordance with applicable Law. Customer shall be responsible and solely liable for all the Content (including without limitation all intellectual property rights therein) and the Properties.

Comment:
[Playbook] We extended the licence to our affiliates and to contractors acting on our behalf, tied revocation to expiration or termination under paragraph 4 rather than Kubient's discretion, and aligned transferability with the assignment right in paragraph 14(h). A licence that is revocable at will and excludes affiliates and contractors is not workable for us operationally.

You are a precise customer-side contract drafter handling one playbook rule.
Use the document tools to inspect only the clauses needed, including definitions and cross-references.
Reason about direction: identify who is bound and do not flag obligations that benefit our party.
Every quote and replace.oldText must be a verbatim substring from a tool response. Quotes must be 600 characters or fewer.
Apply the playbook's classification semantics: a clause that meets the preferred or the fallback position on its material terms is compliant — do not redline it. When a clause genuinely fails the fallback, make the smallest edit that reaches the preferred position; use fallback language only when the rule guidance or the existing bargain makes preferred disproportionate.
Comments must begin with the supplied playbook prefix, use concise first-person-plural language, and explain the change and reason.
For deviation or missing findings, call propose_redline and obtain ok:true before submit_finding.
For compliant findings, do not propose a redline. Call submit_finding exactly once, then stop calling tools.

We represent the customer.
Our party aliases: Customer, Client, Licensee, Company, Buyer, Purchaser, Subscriber, User.
Counterparty aliases: Vendor, Supplier, Provider, Service Provider, Licensor, Contractor, Consultant, Seller, Host.
Comment prefix: [Playbook].
Tone: Concise, professional, first person plural ("we"). Explain what changed and why in one or two sentences, cite the playbook position, offer the fallback where sensible, never lecture.


How to classify a clause against a rule (this is how the reviewing team reads its own playbook):
- compliant: the clause meets the preferred position, OR it meets the fallback position on its material terms. A clause at the fallback is acceptable and is not redlined; say in the rationale that it sits at the fallback.
- deviation: the clause fails the fallback on a material term, or falls into walk-away territory. Only then propose a redline.
- missing: the rule expects a clause and no usable clause exists anywhere in the document.
- Minor sub-elements short of the preferred wording (a missing reminder mechanic, a missing price-uplift cap, 'paid' versus 'paid or payable', an accepted-but-not-preferred governing law) are noted in the rationale, not flagged as deviations.
- Do not flag a clause that benefits our party. Do not flag the same commercial term twice under two rules unless both rules are independently breached.

system.text:
You are a precise customer-side contract drafter handling one playbook rule.
Use the document tools to inspect only the clauses needed, including definitions and cross-references.
Reason about direction: identify who is bound and do not flag obligations that benefit our party.
Every quote and replace.oldText must be a verbatim substring from a tool response. Quotes must be 600 characters or fewer.
Apply the playbook's classification semantics: a clause that meets the preferred or the fallback position on its material terms is compliant — do not redline it. When a clause genuinely fails the fallback, make the smallest edit that reaches the preferred position; use fallback language only when the rule guidance or the existing bargain makes preferred disproportionate.
Comments must begin with the supplied playbook prefix, use concise first-person-plural language, and explain the change and reason.
For deviation or missing findings, call propose_redline and obtain ok:true before submit_finding.
For compliant findings, do not propose a redline. Call submit_finding exactly once, then stop calling tools.

We represent the customer.
Our party aliases: Customer, Client, Licensee, Company, Buyer, Purchaser, Subscriber, User.
Counterparty aliases: Vendor, Supplier, Provider, Service Provider, Licensor, Contractor, Consultant, Seller, Host.
Comment prefix: [Playbook].
Tone: Concise, professional, first person plural ("we"). Explain what changed and why in one or two sentences, cite the playbook position, offer the fallback where sensible, never lecture.


How to classify a clause against a rule (this is how the reviewing team reads its own playbook):
- compliant: the clause meets the preferred position, OR it meets the fallback position on its material terms. A clause at the fallback is acceptable and is not redlined; say in the rationale that it sits at the fallback.
- deviation: the clause fails the fallback on a material term, or falls into walk-away territory. Only then propose a redline.
- missing: the rule expects a clause and no usable clause exists anywhere in the document.
- Minor sub-elements short of the preferred wording (a missing reminder mechanic, a missing price-uplift cap, 'paid' versus 'paid or payable', an accepted-but-not-preferred governing law) are noted in the rationale, not flagged as deviations.
- Do not flag a clause that benefits our party. Do not flag the same commercial term twice under two rules unless both rules are independently breached.

messages.content:
Parties: we represent The Associated Press; counterparty is Kubient Inc..

Rule:
ID: WARRANTY
Title: Performance warranty and duration
Kind: parametric
Summary: The Vendor must stand behind its work for a meaningful period with a real remedy.
Severity: medium
Category: warranty
Position — preferred:
Services performed in a professional and workmanlike manner; deliverables/software conform to documentation for 12 months (software) or 90 days (services) with repair, replace or refund; compliance with laws; no malicious code.

Position — fallback:
90 days for software, 30 days for services; same remedies.
Position — walk-away:
"AS IS" with all warranties disclaimed and no conformance warranty at all.
Detection guidance:
Find warranty and disclaimer sections; extract the warranty period and remedy; note whether the disclaimer swallows the express warranty. A missing express warranty is a deviation (insert).

Redline guidance:
Extend the period, add the remedy sentence, carve the express warranty out of the disclaimer.
Model language:
Vendor warrants that (a) the Services will be performed in a professional and workmanlike manner consistent with industry standards; and (b) for a period of ninety (90) days following delivery, each Deliverable will conform in all material respects to its documentation. Customer's remedy for breach of this warranty is, at Vendor's option, re-performance, repair or replacement, or a refund of the fees paid for the non-conforming Services or Deliverable.

content.text:
**Finding: Compliant** — no redline proposed.

The warranty package in Section 9(b) meets and in places exceeds our preferred position:

- **Performance warranty present**: Service will "perform in all material respects to industry standards" (p0034) and services will be "free from errors that materially affect their utility" (p0038) — the functional equivalent of professional/workmanlike plus conformance.
- **Duration better than preferred**: these are continuing warranties/covenants for the entire Term, not a 12-month or 90-day window.
- **Compliance with laws** (p0041) and **no malicious code** (p0036) are both expressly covered.
- **Disclaimer does not swallow the warranty**: Section 13 is double-qualified ("Except as expressly set forth herein" / "except for the representations and warranties set forth in this Agreement"), so it reaches only implied warranties and the revenue/profit guarantee — nowhere near walk-away "AS IS".

Noted in the rationale but deliberately not flagged: there is no express repair/re-perform/refund remedy sentence. That is a sub-element short of the preferred wording, and its absence favours us — we retain full direct-damages recovery and the 30-day cure/termination right under 4(b) instead of being confined to an exclusive, capped remedy. Inserting the model remedy language would risk narrowing our position, so I left it alone.

input.quote: Either Party may terminate this Agreement for any reason following the Initial Term upon ninety (90) days written notice to the other Party.
input.rationale:
Compliant at the playbook fallback; no redline and no counterparty-facing comment. Reconciling the failed deterministic check first: the check searches for literal "for convenience" wording and therefore misses this clause's formulation, "terminate this Agreement for any reason." A right to terminate "for any reason" is a termination-for-convenience right — it requires no cause, breach, or trigger — so the failure is a phrasing variant, not a missing right. No substantive defect was identified on re-review.

Material terms against T4C: (1) Customer convenience right is present — AP may terminate "for any reason" following the Initial Term on ninety (90) days' written notice, sitting at the outer edge of the fallback's 60–90 day notice window. (2) Term structure — a one (1) year Initial Term with 1-year automatic renewals, so the detection trigger for "absence of any Customer convenience right in a term longer than 12 months" is not met and there is no multi-year lock-in; AP holds a rolling 90-day exit from the end of year one onward. (3) The mid-Initial-Term bar ("Neither Party may terminate this Agreement during the Initial Term") is symmetric and equally prevents Kubient from walking away on AP mid-term, so it operates partly in our favour and is not flagged against us. (4) No early-termination fee or penalty falls on AP — Kubient is entitled only to fees "generated during the termination period," i.e. revenue actually earned while it continues performing across the 90-day notice period, which is within the fallback's 3-months'-fees ceiling. (5) Kubient's convenience right arises only after the Initial Term and on exactly ninety (90) days' notice — not "fewer than 90 days" — so it stays outside walk-away territory.

Sub-elements short of the preferred position, noted rather than escalated per the playbook's classification semantics: 90-day rather than 30-day notice; Kubient's right not confined to the end of a renewal term; and no pro-rata refund of prepaid fees, which is inapplicable because §5 (p0023) is a revenue-share under which funds flow from Kubient to AP within seven (7) days of receipt, so AP prepays no fees capable of refund.

Parties: we represent The Associated Press; counterparty is Kubient Inc..

Rule:
ID: T4C
Title: Termination for convenience
Kind: parametric
Summary: We can leave on notice without penalty; the Vendor cannot walk away mid-term.
Severity: high
Category: term-termination
Position — preferred:
Customer may terminate for convenience on 30 days' written notice with a pro-rata refund of prepaid fees; Vendor has no termination-for-convenience right during a committed term.

Position — fallback:
Customer termination on 60–90 days' notice; early-termination fee not exceeding 3 months' fees; Vendor may terminate for convenience only at the end of a term on 90 days' notice.

Position — walk-away:
No Customer right to terminate for convenience in a multi-year term; Vendor termination for convenience on fewer than 90 days' notice.

Detection guidance:
Find termination provisions. Determine which party may terminate without cause, the notice period, and any early-termination fee. Absence of any Customer convenience right in a term longer than 12 months is a deviation (kind: missing behaviour); a Vendor convenience right on short notice is a deviation.

Redline guidance:
Add or edit a Customer convenience right (30 days), delete/limit Vendor's convenience right, replace penalties with the fallback fee cap.

Model language:
Customer may terminate this Agreement or any Order Form for convenience, in whole or in part, upon thirty (30) days' prior written notice to Vendor, in which case Vendor shall refund any prepaid fees for the period after the effective date of termination.

**Finding: compliant** (no redline proposed)

The Kubient / AP Master Services Agreement contains no audit right running against AP. Searches for "audit", "inspect", "records" and "verif" returned no hits, and a full read of the single-section document confirms it: there is no inspection, verification or records-examination clause anywhere.

Key points:
- The commercial structure is a revenue share flowing **from** Kubient **to** AP under sequential liability (§5, p0023), so there is no AP usage or underpayment for Kubient to audit in the first place.
- The only access-flavoured obligation is §1 (p0001), where AP agrees to provide "reasonable and necessary access, support and cooperation for Kubient to provide the Services." That is a service-enablement covenant, not an audit or verification right, and it gives Kubient no right to examine AP's books or systems.

You are a precise customer-side contract drafter handling one playbook rule.
Use the document tools to inspect only the clauses needed, including definitions and cross-references.
Reason about direction: identify who is bound and do not flag obligations that benefit our party.
Every quote and replace.oldText must be a verbatim substring from a tool response. Quotes must be 600 characters or fewer.
Apply the playbook's classification semantics: a clause that meets the preferred or the fallback position on its material terms is compliant — do not redline it. When a clause genuinely fails the fallback, make the smallest edit that reaches the preferred position; use fallback language only when the rule guidance or the existing bargain makes preferred disproportionate.
Comments must begin with the supplied playbook prefix, use concise first-person-plural language, and explain the change and reason.
For deviation or missing findings, call propose_redline and obtain ok:true before submit_finding.
For compliant findings, do not propose a redline. Call submit_finding exactly once, then stop calling tools.

We represent the customer.
Our party aliases: Customer, Client, Licensee, Company, Buyer, Purchaser, Subscriber, User.
Counterparty aliases: Vendor, Supplier, Provider, Service Provider, Licensor, Contractor, Consultant, Seller, Host.
Comment prefix: [Playbook].
Tone: Concise, professional, first person plural ("we"). Explain what changed and why in one or two sentences, cite the playbook position, offer the fallback where sensible, never lecture.


How to classify a clause against a rule (this is how the reviewing team reads its own playbook):
- compliant: the clause meets the preferred position, OR it meets the fallback position on its material terms. A clause at the fallback is acceptable and is not redlined; say in the rationale that it sits at the fallback.
- deviation: the clause fails the fallback on a material term, or falls into walk-away territory. Only then propose a redline.
- missing: the rule expects a clause and no usable clause exists anywhere in the document.
- Minor sub-elements short of the preferred wording (a missing reminder mechanic, a missing price-uplift cap, 'paid' versus 'paid or payable', an accepted-but-not-preferred governing law) are noted in the rationale, not flagged as deviations.
- Do not flag a clause that benefits our party. Do not flag the same commercial term twice under two rules unless both rules are independently breached.

Title: Minimum purchase commitments and volume restrictions on Customer

No minimum commitment; fees are for usage or ordered services only.

Commitment limited to the current 12-month term, reducible on 30 days' notice, with a true-up rather than a penalty.

Multi-year take-or-pay commitments with no reduction or termination right.

"minimum", "commit to purchase", "take or pay", "shortfall", volume caps on Customer usage. Commitments the Vendor makes to us are fine.

Delete or narrow to the fallback with minimal edits; replace shortfall penalties with a true-up.

input.quote: 14. General Provisions.
input.rationale: A full-text search for "insurance"/coverage returns nothing, and a read of the entire Agreement (single Preamble section, p0000–p0074, including the General Provisions in section 14) confirms there is no insurance obligation on either Party, nor any Exhibit reference to coverage. Kubient is a hosting/services vendor: it hosts the Auction Platform (p0002), receives Requests data from Customer (p0011), and expressly warrants that it collects, maintains, manages and stores visitor information/data (p0035(iii)). A vendor that processes personal/visitor data with no insurance at all is walk-away territory under this rule, so this is a missing-clause deviation rather than a fallback position. We propose inserting a short insurance paragraph as new section 14(j) at the preferred limits (CGL USD 1M per occurrence / USD 2M aggregate, E&O USD 2M, cyber USD 5M where Kubient processes our or visitor data, workers' compensation as required by Law, certificates on request), with the fallback (E&O USD 1M / cyber USD 2M) offered in the comment. Severity is low and the insertion is one paragraph in the miscellaneous section, so no other terms are disturbed.

ops.text: (j) Insurance. Kubient shall maintain, at its own expense, throughout the Term and for one (1) year thereafter: commercial general liability insurance of not less than USD 1,000,000 per occurrence and USD 2,000,000 in the aggregate; professional liability (errors and omissions) insurance of not less than USD 2,000,000; and, where Kubient collects, processes or stores Customer or visitor data, cyber liability insurance of not less than USD 5,000,000. Kubient shall also maintain workers' compensation insurance as required by applicable Law, and shall provide certificates of insurance to Customer on request.

These are our standard limits (CGL USD 1M/2M, E&O USD 2M, cyber USD 5M); if helpful we can discuss E&O of USD 1M and cyber of USD 2M as a fallback.

How to classify a clause against a rule (this is how the reviewing team reads its own playbook):
- compliant: the clause meets the preferred position, OR it meets the fallback position on its material terms. A clause at the fallback is acceptable and is not redlined; say in the rationale that it sits at the fallback.
- deviation: the clause fails the fallback on a material term, or falls into walk-away territory. Only then propose a redline.
- missing: the rule expects a clause and no usable clause exists anywhere in the document.
- Minor sub-elements short of the preferred wording (a missing reminder mechanic, a missing price-uplift cap, 'paid' versus 'paid or payable', an accepted-but-not-preferred governing law) are noted in the rationale, not flagged as deviations.

Parties: we represent The Associated Press; counterparty is Kubient Inc..

Rule:
ID: INSURANCE
Title: Vendor insurance
Kind: missing
Summary: Vendors that touch our data or premises carry standard insurance.
Severity: low
Category: insurance
Position — preferred:
Commercial general liability USD 1M per occurrence / 2M aggregate; professional (E&O) USD 2M; cyber/privacy USD 5M for vendors processing Customer Data; workers' compensation as required by law; certificates on request.

Position — fallback:
E&O USD 1M and cyber USD 2M.
Position — walk-away:
No insurance for a vendor that processes personal data or works on our premises.
Detection guidance:
Look for an insurance clause; if absent for a services/hosting vendor, deviation (insert).
Redline guidance:
Insert a short insurance paragraph in the general/miscellaneous section.
Model language:
Vendor shall maintain, at its own expense, throughout the term and for one (1) year thereafter: commercial general liability insurance of not less than USD 1,000,000 per occurrence and USD 2,000,000 in the aggregate; professional liability (errors and omissions) insurance of not less than USD 2,000,000; and, where Vendor processes Customer Data, cyber liability insurance of not less than USD 5,000,000. Vendor shall provide certificates of insurance on request.

input.rationale: A full-text search for "insurance"/coverage returns nothing, and a read of the entire Agreement (single Preamble section, p0000–p0074, including the General Provisions in section 14) confirms there is no insurance obligation on either Party, nor any Exhibit reference to coverage. Kubient is a hosting/services vendor: it hosts the Auction Platform (p0002), receives Requests data from Customer (p0011), and expressly warrants that it collects, maintains, manages and stores visitor information/data (p0035(iii)). A vendor that processes personal/visitor data with no insurance at all is walk-away territory under this rule, so this is a missing-clause deviation rather than a fallback position. We propose inserting a short insurance paragraph as new section 14(j) at the preferred limits (CGL USD 1M per occurrence / USD 2M aggregate, E&O USD 2M, cyber USD 5M where Kubient processes our or visitor data, workers' compensation as required by Law, certificates on request), with the fallback (E&O USD 1M / cyber USD 2M) offered in the comment. Severity is low and the insertion is one paragraph in the miscellaneous section, so no other terms are disturbed.

messages.content:
Rule:
ID: T4C
Title: Termination for convenience
Kind: parametric
Summary: We can leave on notice without penalty; the Vendor cannot walk away mid-term.
Severity: high
Category: term-termination
Position — preferred:
Customer may terminate for convenience on 30 days' written notice with a pro-rata refund of prepaid fees; Vendor has no termination-for-convenience right during a committed term.

Position — fallback:
Customer termination on 60–90 days' notice; early-termination fee not exceeding 3 months' fees; Vendor may terminate for convenience only at the end of a term on 90 days' notice.

Position — walk-away:
No Customer right to terminate for convenience in a multi-year term; Vendor termination for convenience on fewer than 90 days' notice.

Detection guidance:
Find termination provisions. Determine which party may terminate without cause, the notice period, and any early-termination fee. Absence of any Customer convenience right in a term longer than 12 months is a deviation (kind: missing behaviour); a Vendor convenience right on short notice is a deviation.

Redline guidance:
Add or edit a Customer convenience right (30 days), delete/limit Vendor's convenience right, replace penalties with the fallback fee cap.

Model language:
Customer may terminate this Agreement or any Order Form for convenience, in whole or in part, upon thirty (30) days' prior written notice to Vendor, in which case Vendor shall refund any prepaid fees for the period after the effective date of termination.


Claimed finding status: compliant

Finding rationale:
Compliant at the playbook fallback; no redline and no counterparty-facing comment. Reconciling the failed deterministic check first: the check searches for literal "for convenience" wording and therefore misses this clause's formulation, "terminate this Agreement for any reason." A right to terminate "for any reason" is a termination-for-convenience right — it requires no cause, breach, or trigger — so the failure is a phrasing variant, not a missing right. No substantive defect was identified on re-review.

Material terms against T4C: (1) Customer convenience right is present — AP may terminate "for any reason" following the Initial Term on ninety (90) days' written notice, sitting at the outer edge of the fallback's 60–90 day notice window. (2) Term structure — a one (1) year Initial Term with 1-year automatic renewals, so the detection trigger for "absence of any Customer convenience right in a term longer than 12 months" is not met and there is no multi-year lock-in; AP holds a rolling 90-day exit from the end of year one onward. (3) The mid-Initial-Term bar ("Neither Party may terminate this Agreement during the Initial Term") is symmetric and equally prevents Kubient from walking away on AP mid-term, so it operates partly in our favour and is not flagged against us. (4) No early-termination fee or penalty falls on AP — Kubient is entitled only to fees "generated during the termination period," i.e. revenue actually earned while it continues performing across the 90-day notice period, which is within the fallback's 3-months'-fees ceiling. (5) Kubient's convenience right arises only after the Initial Term and on exactly ninety (90) days' notice — not "fewer than 90 days" — so it stays outside walk-away territory.

Sub-elements short of the preferred position, noted rather than escalated per the playbook's classification semantics: 90-day rather than 30-day notice; Kubient's right not confined to the end of a renewal term; and no pro-rata refund of prepaid fees, which is inapplicable because §5 (p0023) is a revenue-share under which funds flow from Kubient to AP within seven (7) days of receipt, so AP prepays no fees capable of refund.

This Agreement will automatically renew for additional 1-year terms unless earlier terminated pursuant to this Agreement's express provisions (together with the Initial Term, such additional periods the "Term"). **Final finding: compliant** — no redline, no counterparty comment.

No repair was warranted this round. Every substantive bullet in the verifier feedback affirmed the finding:

- **Classification correct** — the rule caps a Vendor-favourable audit right; its total absence is better than the preferred position, so compliant (not deviation, not missing).
- **Cited text supports it** — Section 1 (p0001) is a service-enablement cooperation covenant, with no right to examine AP's books, usage or systems and no remote/system-access grant.
- **Output shape correct** — no redline rendered, no comment proposed, document unmodified.
- **Rationale accurate** — including the residual note on Exhibits.

The only failing item is the deterministic `audit frequency limited` check, which the verifier itself characterises as a false signal: it fails because there is *no* audit clause to carry a frequency cap, not because audits are unlimited or unannounced. I deliberately did not chase that check green, because the only way to do so would be to insert audit frequency/notice/cost parameters — which would manufacture a Kubient audit right against AP that the Agreement does not currently contain. That would be a directionally wrong edit against our own client's interest.

Carried forward as an internal watch item rather than a negotiation ask: Exhibits are incorporated into the Agreement under Section 1, so if a future Exhibit or amendment introduces audit or system-access language, we should require the preferred parameters then (once per 12 months, 30 days' written notice, independent auditor bound by confidentiality, Kubient's cost unless underpayment exceeds 5%, no direct access to AP systems).

Stopping here — the finding is submitted and I will not call further tools on this rule.

Judge the proposal against the supplied playbook rule, original paragraphs, resolved definitions, deterministic checks, rendered redline, and comment.
Do not rely on hidden drafter reasoning. Fail invalid, directionally wrong, or rule-incomplete edits.
Deterministic checks are heuristics (regular expressions and a changed-character ratio), not verdicts: a failed regex may simply be a phrasing variant, and a high changed-character ratio is acceptable when the rule genuinely requires rewriting the clause (for example replacing a governing-law sentence or deleting a take-or-pay obligation). Weigh them as evidence and decide on substance: does the redline reach the playbook position with the smallest edit that does so, and is the comment accurate?
The claimed status matters: for a compliant finding, no redline or counterparty comment is expected, and you should pass when the cited text supports compliance. Fail a deviation finding whose cited clause already meets the preferred or the fallback position on its material terms (the playbook's classification semantics) — a redline that merely upgrades an acceptable fallback to preferred wording is over-flagging. Compliant findings are retained as internal evaluation evidence, not raised as negotiation issues. For deviation or missing findings, require an actionable valid proposal.
Return a concise verdict with actionable reasons.

How to classify a clause against a rule (this is how the reviewing team reads its own playbook):
- compliant: the clause meets the preferred position, OR it meets the fallback position on its material terms. A clause at the fallback is acceptable and is not redlined; say in the rationale that it sits at the fallback.
